analyst_view.overall: Early view: This is Tenerife's first match since striker Jesús de Miguel died on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra's goalkeeper at the Heliodoro; their game at Granada was postponed and the club held a public tribute at the stadium on 7 November, so the emotional context outweighs anything in the numbers. Álvaro Cervera's side had drawn four in a row before that, while bottom club Ceuta (five points, 30 goals conceded) have lost five straight and, per one report, appointed Sergio Lobera on 8 November, so this is likely his first game in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I stay close to it. Ceuta concede more than two a game, which points up, but Tenerife have been a draw team (three 1-1s and a 2-2 in a row) and an emotionally heavy day is hard to read. Lobera's first aim will probably be a more organised Ceuta.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners and I leave it. Tenerife should have more of the territory against a side that has lost five in a row, but the site already gives them the larger share, and a new coach's first priority is usually to make his team compact.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. I lean lower: in the first game at the Heliodoro since the club's tribute to De Miguel, I expect both teams to avoid flashpoints, and Ceuta under a brand-new coach are unlikely to start with a niggly approach. Dani Martín's suspension (listed by the site) also removes one Tenerife booking risk.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.7 shots. I lean higher: Ceuta have conceded 30 goals in 13 games, the most in the division, and lost 0-3 at Córdoba last weekend, so Tenerife's 11.9 looks low against the league's worst defence.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. I lean higher, driven by Tenerife's side: Ceuta's defence has been breached 30 times and Enric Gallego has eight goals. Ceuta's share should stay modest; they have scored once in their last three league games.
